I found a valid assignment with total spill cost 20. I did not prove it optimal, but every alternative I explored cost 21 or more.

**Forced colors.** Precolored neighbours restrict the other nodes heavily. Nodes 5, 11, 12, 14 and 28 each touch precolored nodes with colors 0, 1 and 2, so each is forced to color 3 if kept.

**Mandatory spills.**
- Nodes 11 and 14 are adjacent and both forced to 3, and 14 and 28 are adjacent and both forced to 3. Spilling 14 (cost 3) fixes both.
- Nodes 9, 28 and 29 lie in the 5-clique {7, 9, 27, 28, 29}, and 28, 22 and 29 form a triangle with 22 and 29 each limited to {0, 3}. Spilling 28 (cost 7) fixes both. Covering them any other way costs at least 11.
- Nodes 5, 6 and 10 conflict with each other and with precolored 4 and 7. Spilling 10 (cost 3) is the cheapest fix.

**Forced chain after those spills.** Nodes 6, 13 and 29 are forced to 0. Nodes 8, 18, 19, 20, 23 and 25 are all forced to 1. Nodes 15 and 26 are both forced to 2. These force clashes on the adjacent pairs 8-23, 8-25, 18-20, 19-20, 19-25, 20-23 and 15-26. The cheapest cover of those pairs is {20, 23, 25, 15}, costing 2 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 7.

**Total.** The spilled set is {28, 14, 10, 25, 20, 23, 15}, with cost 7 + 3 + 3 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 20.

**Alternatives tried.** Spilling 5 instead of 10 gives 21. Spilling 11 instead of 14 gives a worse clash set. Keeping 28 and spilling 9 and 22 instead costs more. Spilling 12 or 13 as well does not remove the 8-23 clash.
